voiceover: More than two centuries before the council of 325, one bishop wrote a single sentence about Jesus. His name was Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, in the generation after the apostles. Around the years 107 to 110, he wrote seven letters while being marched under guard to his execution in Rome. To the church at Ephesus, he wrote: For our God, Jesus Christ, was, according to the appointment of God, conceived in the womb by Mary, of the seed of David, but by the Holy Ghost. He calls Jesus our God, without apology or argument — and in the same breath, born of Mary, of the seed of David. A man writing on his way to be eaten by beasts is not polishing an archive for posterity. He is recording the settled speech of his churches. So the council of 325 did not invent the divinity of Jesus. It defended an inherited faith, rather than manufacturing a novelty.
